steps.title: First identify what owns the motion
steps.explanation: This mannequin starts in an authored neutral pose. Its graph and bound surface describe geometry; they supply neither measured anatomy nor a force law. Orbit the camera without changing the pose.
steps.observe: The view changes while the prescribed pose remains neutral. Force, pressure and contact response are not modeled.

steps.title: Move a coordinate frame without deforming the body
steps.explanation: Translate the root by 0.4 scene units in the poser’s horizontal direction. Every local pose coordinate stays the same, so a moved silhouette alone cannot establish tissue strain or mechanical work.
steps.observe: The whole character moves together; the pose graph and skin shape are unchanged. This is a prescribed placement, not acceleration under force.

steps.title: Change pose, then ask for the missing law
steps.explanation: The existing hand-on-torso test prescribes a right-hand target and elbow pole. Inverse kinematics chooses bone positions and geometric skinning follows them. A tissue model would additionally need a material law, boundaries, forces and convergence checks.
steps.observe: The arm bends toward the torso. The pose does not produce contact pressure or an equilibrium residual; these outputs remain not modeled.

audit.finding: The opening example was an unstructured poser with no worked state or quantities separating camera, placement and deformation.
audit.change: Three bounded presets introduce view inspection, rigid placement and prescribed IK; unavailable physical outputs are explicit.
audit.remaining: The poser supplies no anatomical calibration, collision response, tissue strain measurement or biomechanics.
